title: Phytochemically engineered  Nigella sativa  silver nanoparticles induce apoptosis in hepatocellular carcinoma and inhibit pathogenic growth
content: This study evaluates the green biosynthesis, material characterization, antimicrobial potential, and in vitro anticancer mechanism of silver nanoparticles (AgNPs) synthesized using Nigella sativa (black seed) aqueous extract. The biogenic nanoparticles were characterized using UV-Vis spectrophotometry, Fourier-transform infrared spectroscopy (FTIR), X-ray diffraction (XRD), Field Emission Scanning Electron Microscopy (FESEM), and Energy-Dispersive X-ray (EDX) microanalysis. Characterization confirmed the formation of spherical, face-centered cubic crystalline silver nanoparticles with an average size of 50–70 nm and a characteristic surface plasmon resonance peak at 420–430 nm. Biogenic AgNPs displayed exceptional antimicrobial efficacy via agar well diffusion assays, yielding distinct zones of inhibition against Staphylococcus aureus (22.0 mm), Escherichia coli (24.0 mm), and Candida auris (18.0 mm), systematically outperforming standard clinical antibiotic and antifungal controls. Furthermore, in vitro cytotoxicity evaluation via MTT assay against human hepatocellular carcinoma cells (HepG2) demonstrated a significant reduction in cellular metabolic viability with an IC50 value of 5.0 µg mL−1, presenting a highly potent, concentration-dependent profile comparable to the standard chemotherapeutic drug Doxorubicin (IC50 ∼7.99 µg mL−1). Furthermore, 48-hour colorimetric MTT metabolic assays demonstrated a pronounced, dose-dependent cytotoxic effect against human hepatocellular carcinoma (HepG2) cells. The half-maximal inhibitory concentration IC50 was established at a low threshold of 5.0 µg mL−1, presenting a highly potent cytotoxic profile comparable to the clinical chemotherapy standard doxorubicin. Inverted light microscopy confirmed a complete breakdown of confluent HepG2 cell monolayers into isolated, highly contracted spherical cell clusters at the IC50 mark. Downstream Annexin V-FITC/PI flow cytometry analysis validated that the anti-proliferative activity was driven by the activation of programmed cell death pathways rather than non-specific mechanical necrosis. As concentrations escalated to a high saturation dose (10.0 µg mL−1), the viable cell pool plummeted to 26.16%, while early apoptotic events maximized significantly to 40.54% (p < 0.001). These single-cell dynamics confirm that Nigella sativa-mediated AgNPs function as potent anti-proliferative agents, providing a scalable and highly active platform for advanced biomedical and hepatic oncology investigations.
